scopes.core: Product, platform and standards repositories adopting the stack.
scopes.experimental: Hackathon and guild repositories: proxied by the cache, not bound by the single stack.

node.note: Node 26 is Current until it becomes Active LTS on 2026-10-28; Node 24 entered Maintenance on 2026-10-20. Node 26.12.1 bundles npm 11.20.0; standalone npm latest is 12.2.1.

bun.note: Primary JS/TS package manager and runtime per playbook-dev-devices.

python.reason: Owner selects both lines. 3.15 is the latest; 3.14 is admitted for projects whose locked set does not resolve on 3.15. The core whole-set uv resolution succeeds on 3.14 and fails on 3.15 (ctranslate2/faster-whisper publish no cp315 wheels; livekit-agents requires <3.15).
python.removal_condition: The 3.14 line stays while any core project needs it; re-run the core resolution on 3.15 after CTranslate2 publishes cp315 wheels and livekit-agents allows 3.15.

typescript.reason: Owner selects TypeScript 7 (native compiler) and the latest TypeScript 6 (JavaScript compiler API for typescript-eslint, openapi-typescript, @astrojs/check, svelte-language-server). The @typescript/typescript6 alias package currently publishes 6.0.2; alias npm:typescript@6.0.3 instead.
typescript.removal_condition: The TypeScript 6 line stays until typescript-eslint, openapi-typescript and @astrojs/check run on TypeScript 7.

jdk.reason: Owner selects the latest feature release and the latest LTS. Gradle runs on JDK 27 only from 9.8.0; with the Kotlin-compatible Gradle line use JDK 25. Kotlin 2.4.21 -jvm-target stops at 26 and Flutter 3.47.8 treats Java >=26 as newer-than-known, so Android/Flutter apps keep Java target 17.
jdk.note: playbook-dev-devices installs JDK 27 and JDK 21 (jvm-lts); the LTS line it installs needs to move to 25.
jdk.removal_condition: None for the two-line policy; the Java 17 app target follows Flutter/Kotlin support for newer targets.

gradle.reason: Owner selects the latest Gradle and the newest Gradle fully supported by Kotlin Gradle Plugin 2.4.21 (Gradle 7.6.3-9.7.0; 9.7.1 is its bug-fix patch). Kotlin/Android builds use the compatible line.
gradle.removal_condition: A Kotlin Gradle Plugin release that lists Gradle >=9.8 makes the latest line sufficient.

android-gradle-plugin.reason: The owner's Gradle rule applied to AGP: the latest release and the newest release fully supported by Kotlin Gradle Plugin 2.4.21 (AGP 8.5.2-9.3.1; 9.3.3 is a bug-fix patch). AGP 9.4 requires Gradle >=9.6.0.
android-gradle-plugin.removal_condition: A Kotlin Gradle Plugin release that lists AGP >=9.4.

android-sdk.stack: platform android-37.0 (compileSdk/targetSdk 37), build-tools 37.0.0 (set buildToolsVersion explicitly; AGP default is 36.0.0), cmdline-tools 23.0, NDK 30.0.16248370
android-sdk.reason: Upstream latest platform is 37.2 (minor API); AGP 9.3 documents API 37 and Flutter reads compileSdk as an integer; 37.1/37.2 unverified. NDK r30 is the latest LTS and already used by a core repo, but AGP 9.x and Flutter 3.47.8 default to 28.2.13676358 (fallback).
android-sdk.removal_condition: AGP and Flutter document support for minor API platforms (37.1/37.2) and NDK r30.

flutter_rust_bridge_codegen.note: Must equal crate flutter_rust_bridge 2.13.0 and pub flutter_rust_bridge 2.13.0.

vector.reason: A project keeps its qualified 0.59.0 journald compatibility image until an upstream release fixes the idle disk-buffer flush; 0.60.0 does not contain the fix, so it does not justify requalification.
vector.removal_condition: An upstream release contains the idle disk-buffer flush fix and the project's cold-first-event, privacy, restart and outage acceptance passes on it.

ubuntu.reason: Release binaries for runtimes on Ubuntu 24.04 must link against glibc 2.39 or older, so their build image stays on Ubuntu 24.04 with a GLIBC symbol gate; current Rust toolchains run on it.
ubuntu.removal_condition: The target runtime moves to a newer ABI by plan and every release binary passes its check there.

eslint.reason: eslint-config-next 16.4.3 (latest) depends on eslint-plugin-react 7.37, eslint-plugin-import 2.32 and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10, whose latest releases peer eslint <=9.
eslint.alternative: ESLint 10.13.0 only in repositories without those plugins, or replace them with Biome/oxlint.
eslint.removal_condition: eslint-config-next and its bundled plugins release peer ranges that include ESLint 10.

@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base.reason: Kept on the OpenTelemetry JS 2.x line together with @vercel/otel.

@opentelemetry/exporter-logs-otlp-http.reason: @vercel/otel 2.1.3 peers @opentelemetry/sdk-logs <0.300.0, and exporter-logs-otlp-http 0.300.0 depends on sdk-logs 3.0.0.

boto3.reason: aioboto3 15.5.0 (latest) pins aiobotocore 2.25.1, which requires boto3 <1.40.62 (one core project).
boto3.removal_condition: aioboto3 releases with aiobotocore 3.x, or the affected project replaces aioboto3.

replacements.npm:@react-email/components: Package marked no longer supported by npm.
replacements.pypi:miniopy-async: Stale and MinIO-specific; use an S3 client against RustFS.
replacements.image:minio: minio/minio GitHub repository archived; RustFS is already used by the company stack.

workspace_rules.rule: Do not combine sqlx 0.9.x with rusqlite 0.41.x / sqlite-wasm-rs 0.6.x in one Cargo workspace: sqlx-sqlite bounds libsqlite3-sys <0.38 and Cargo enforces links="sqlite3" even for sqlx's optional sqlite backend. A shared workspace must use rusqlite 0.39.0 + sqlite-wasm-rs 0.5.5.
workspace_rules.verified: cargo generate-lockfile probe with all crates =latest failed; succeeded with rusqlite 0.39.0 + sqlite-wasm-rs 0.5.5
workspace_rules.removal_condition: sqlx (now transact-rs/sqlx) releases with a libsqlite3-sys bound that includes the version used by the latest rusqlite. No upstream issue found.

isolated_tools.pypi:semgrep: Install as an isolated tool (uv tool); it pins click, jsonschema, mcp and OpenTelemetry exactly.

owner_constraints.cache_implementation: No paid or proprietary products. Use an NDS Rust implementation or open-source components written in Rust.
owner_constraints.network: Internal network only; key-based access for every client.
owner_constraints.consumers: Owner devices and private self-hosted GitHub Actions runners. Public repositories keep free GitHub-hosted runners.
